**Course Catalog**

**0431234 The Foundations of Oration & Call**  
(3 Credit Hours)  
This course discusses the main issues of Islamic Call, such as: the meaning of Islamic Call, its characteristics, rules and importance. This includes: The Caller and his role, the rights of those whom are called, how to assure their faith and morals, an applied study to the main styles of the Call, such as delivering the speech of Jumu’ah, and other circles and lectures which eventually form the best preachers and callers.

---

**0431313 Legislation Verses**  
(3 Credit Hours)  
This course discusses the explanation of the Qur'an's verses of legislation and regulation; survey of evidence provided by scholars; lawful and unlawful matters; verses from chapters: al-Baqarah, al-Nisa, al-Ma'idah, al-Nur, al-Ahzab will be discussed. There are three main points to be taken into consideration, those include: the explanation of these verses, the way of producing rules from these verses and the reasons of Scholars’ differences (if found) and how to deal with them.

---

**0431332 Comparative Religions**  
(3 Credit Hours)  
The object of this course is to provide a comparative study for the revealed religions, al-Adyan al-Samawiyyah, i.e., Christianity and Judaism and for some other religions, such as Hinduism and Buddhism. This course aims also to enable the student to know the most important issues which relate to the creed and to the private legislation of these religions in comparison with Islam. Moreover, it aims to give the student an ability to compare between the main issues of these religions.

---

**0431333 Modern Thoughtful Opinions**  
(3 Credit Hours)  
This course aims to throw light on the main thoughtful trends which invaded our Islamic World, the Islamic attitude from them in order to protect our students from them and how to deal with them. This course includes the manners of invasion of western thought of the Islamic World; such as: Secularism, Nationalism, Communism, Marxism, Pragmatism, etc.

---

**0431433 Islamic Sects**  
(3 Credit Hours)  
The course discusses the development of Islamic sects; the most important sects; their history; dangers of sects on the Islamic unity; their thoughts; the discussion of: Qadariyyah, Jabriyah, Mu'tazilites, Shi'ites, Kharijites, Murji'ah, Isma'ilites, Nusayriy yah, Duruz, Baha'is and Qadyanis.
